title: torch.quantile's float64-rank fallback is hardcoded to MPS instead of using device capabilities
body:
> Note: this issue body was drafted with the help of an AI assistant and reviewed before submission.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`torch.quantile` computes ranks in float64 where the device supports it (lifting the exact-representable float32 size cap from 2^24 to 2^53), and falls back to float32 ranks otherwise. Whether the device supports double is hardcoded to the MPS device type rather than queried from the device's reported capabilities:

`aten/src/ATen/native/Sorting.cpp`, `quantile_compute`:
```cpp
const bool double_ranks =
    self.scalar_type() == kDouble || self.device().type() != at::kMPS;
```

PyTorch already provides a device-polymorphic mechanism for exactly this -- `DeviceGuardImplInterface::getDeviceCapability` / `c10::DeviceCapability`, with per-backend bitfields such as `capability_data.supported_scalar_types.has_Double` -- but `quantile` does not use it. As a consequence, any accelerator backend that does not support double but is not MPS incorrectly takes the float64-rank path and fails, instead of falling back to float32 ranks as MPS does.

This is not only theoretical for custom backends:
- XPU registers device capabilities dynamically per device (`c10/xpu/impl/XPUGuardImpl.h`, `getDeviceCapability`), and only sets the Double bit when `device.has(sycl::aspect::fp64)`. Consumer-grade Intel iGPUs / Arc GPUs that lack the fp64 hardware aspect report no Double support, yet `quantile`'s `!= kMPS` check routes them onto the float64-rank path, where they fail instead of falling back to float32 ranks.
- A `PrivateUse1` backend with fp64 storage but no fp64 compute hits the same path.

The same MPS hardcoding is duplicated in the test `test_quantile_size_limit` (`test/test_reductions.py`), which branches on `self.device_type == "mps"` instead of on the device's reported double support.

### Minimal repro

On an MPS machine the float32-rank cap is honored (the hardcoded case):
```python
import torch
dev = "mps"
# 2^24 is fine (float32 ranks exact to 2^24)
torch.quantile(torch.empty(1 << 24, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev), 0.5)
# past the cap raises, because MPS falls back to float32 ranks (2^24 cap)
over_cap = (1 << 24) + 1
torch.quantile(torch.empty(over_cap, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev), 0.5)
# RuntimeError: quantile() input tensor is too large ...
```
This raise is gated by a literal `device_type == "mps"` check. The equivalent fallback is not triggered for a non-MPS accelerator that likewise lacks double support, because the check is type-based rather than capability-based. On XPU hardware without the fp64 aspect, the past-cap call would similarly take the float64-rank path instead of falling back.

OS: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64)
Python version: 3.12.3

title: [c10d][NCCL] Uneven all_gather_into_tensor / reduce_scatter_tensor that can use NCCL symmetric memory
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Add split-size-aware variants of `all_gather_into_tensor` and `reduce_scatter_tensor`
  (for example `output_split_sizes` / `input_split_sizes`), and let the NCCL backend run 
them on window-registered (symmetric) memory.

  **Motivation.** In Megatron-FSDP we are adding an owner-based sharding mode
  (NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#7396) where each parameter is assigned whole to one rank, so the
  per-rank shard sizes are intentionally unequal and we do not want to pad them to the
  largest shard. Materialization needs an uneven `Shard -> Replicate` all-gather and gradient
  reduction needs an uneven `Partial -> Shard` reduce-scatter.

  Today the only way to express this is the list variants `dist.all_gather` /
  `dist.reduce_scatter`. With unequal sizes `ProcessGroupNCCL` lowers them to a coalesced
  group of per-rank `ncclBroadcast` / `ncclReduce` calls, so they never hit the NCCL
  symmetric-memory kernels that `all_gather_into_tensor` / `reduce_scatter_tensor` get
  when the buffers come from `torch.distributed._symmetric_memory` with the NCCL backend.
  We therefore have to disable symmetric memory whenever the layout is uneven, and lose
  its latency benefit exactly for the sharding mode where communication is most irregular.

 **Why the existing `symm_mem` offset ops do not cover this.** Both assume every rank
  contributes the same amount of data; their "uneven" dimension is across parameters or
  blocks, not across ranks.
  - `symm_mem.all_gather_offset` (#187642, from #187239): `split_sizes[i]` is the
    per-rank shard size of parameter `i`, the same list on every rank, and `out.numel()`
    must equal `sum(split_sizes) * W`. There is no per-rank dimension, so a parameter that
    is whole on one rank and absent on the others cannot be expressed.
  - `symm_mem.reduce_scatter_offset` (#177791): host checks require every rank to own the
    same number of blocks (`n_owned * group_size == n_blocks`) and the `j`-th owned block
    to have the same size on every rank. Owner-packed segments violate both.

  **Pitch.**
  1. Extend `all_gather_into_tensor` / `reduce_scatter_tensor` (or add `*_uneven` siblings)
     with per-rank split sizes along dim 0.
  2. In `ProcessGroupNCCL`, keep the registered-window fast path for these calls instead of 
      falling back to coalesced per-rank broadcast / reduce.

Alternatives:
  - Pad every rank's shard to the largest one and use the uniform collectives: wastes
    memory and bandwidth proportional to the imbalance, and forces padding into the
    optimizer / checkpoint layout.
  - Keep using the list variants with coalesced broadcast/reduce (what we do now):
    correct, but cannot use symmetric memory and issues `world_size` small kernels per
    collective.

Additional context:
  - torch 2.13.0a0 (NGC PyTorch 26.07), NCCL 2.30.7, H100.
  - Consumer: NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#7396 (TensorAtomic placement for MFSDP v2); tracking
    issue for uneven communication: NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#6587.
  - Related: #187239, #187642 (`all_gather_offset`), #177791 (`reduce_scatter_offset`).

### Alternatives

_No response_

title: [inductor] lerp with a weight >= 0.5 returns end's strides, and x.lerp_(end, 0.75); x.view(-1) fails to compile (regression)
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

With a weight of 0.5 or more, `lerp` under `torch.compile` returns `end`'s strides instead of eager's, and a `view` of the result then fails to compile. 2.13, 2.14 and the 21 Sep nightly, CPU and CUDA.

```python
import torch


def f(x, end):
    x.lerp_(end, 0.75)
    return x.view(-1)


x = torch.rand(4, 16, 16)
end = torch.rand(4, 16, 16).transpose(-1, -2)
print(torch.lerp(x, end, 0.75).stride())
print(torch.compile(torch.lerp)(x, end, 0.75).stride())
print(f(x.clone(), end).shape)
print(torch.compile(f)(x.clone(), end).shape)
```

```
(256, 16, 1)
(256, 1, 16)
torch.Size([1024])
torch._dynamo.exc.BackendCompilerFailed: backend='inductor' raised:
ValueError: Cannot view a tensor with shape torch.Size([4, 16, 16]) and strides (256, 1, 16) as a tensor with shape (1024,)!
```

`torch.lerp(x, end, torch.tensor(0.75))` and `torch._foreach_lerp_([x], [end], 0.75)` (float32 and bfloat16) do the same.

I think it comes from the decompositions added in #176804: with |weight| >= 0.5 they start from `end` (`torch.add(end, diff, ...)`, `addcmul(where(mask, end, start), ...)`, `_foreach_addcmul(end_tensors, ...)`), so the result takes end's layout. The `suggest_memory_format(start)` conversion there covers a channels_last `start` but not a transposed `end`. With those entries taken out of the decomposition table, 2.14 gives eager's strides again.

Copying the result onto `empty_like(start)` in those branches, when `start` has the output's shape, fixes all of these on 2.14, CPU and CUDA, also for a `start` with gaps like `x[..., ::2]`. I have it with tests and can open a PR.

title: Cannot initialise process group on CPU device with GLOO backend
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

From the documentation page on `torch.distributed` (https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.html), it seems like with the `gloo` backend, you should be able to initialise a distributed process group on CPU. However, when trying to do this, you actually get a `ValueError: init_process_group device_id parameter must be an accelerator with an index` error.

In particular, if you run:
```
import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
import os

os.environ["RANK"] = "0"
os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"] = "1"
os.environ["MASTER_ADDR"] = "localhost"
os.environ["MASTER_PORT"] = "12345"

dist.init_process_group(backend=dist.Backend.GLOO, device_id=torch.device("cpu:0"), rank=0)
```

then you get
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<python-input-0>", line 10, in <module>
    dist.init_process_group(backend=dist.Backend.GLOO, device_id=torch.device("cpu:0"), rank=0)
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/anaconda3/envs/e2e-ef/lib/python3.13/site-packages/torch/distributed/c10d_logger.py", line 81, in wrapper
    return func(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/opt/anaconda3/envs/e2e-ef/lib/python3.13/site-packages/torch/distributed/c10d_logger.py", line 95, in wrapper
    func_return = func(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/opt/anaconda3/envs/e2e-ef/lib/python3.13/site-packages/torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py", line 1765, in init_process_group
    default_pg, _ = _new_process_group_helper(
                    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^
        world_size,
        ^^^^^^^^^^^
    ...<8 lines>...
        group_desc="default_pg",
        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    )
    ^
  File "/opt/anaconda3/envs/e2e-ef/lib/python3.13/site-packages/torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py", line 1880, in _new_process_group_helper
    raise ValueError(
        "init_process_group device_id parameter must be an accelerator with an index"
    )
ValueError: init_process_group device_id parameter must be an accelerator with an index
```

It seems like the issue is that in `dist.init_process_group`, with the GLOO backend, you end up calling the `_new_process_group_helper` with passing in the `device_id` and that function raises this error as we're calling with a CPU device. 
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/eaa5d9d3d3dc642832b269b184f0c3ab8c990274/torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py#L1764C25-L1775

Happy to try make a PR with some guidance on what to change to make this work
